{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZjhxEw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDKQZA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 119, "title": "Add evidence-qualified multi-recipient local resident mail", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `7c36f48faad24b4751a0be944dc2e96a3e1329de`, each mail composition resolves one destination and `createHumanMail` persists one letter. Users cannot compose one invitation or update for several familiar residents.

This is an existing fidelity omission, not a demonstrated regression from PR #118. NEC's contemporary account documents simultaneous mail distribution, making this a useful next service journey.

## Expected outcome

Support this terminal journey from MAIN `1`, MAIN `X` and DAISIZEN `MAIL`:

`WRITE-MULTI → select distinct local residents → compose once → review all recipients and text → edit/approve/cancel → SENT → READ each saved copy → reload or restore`

Use a separate, explicitly reconstructed `WRITE-MULTI` command. Collect one existing local resident address per input line; `.END` completes selection after at least two distinct residents. Preserve existing single-recipient WRITE/COMPOSE parsing, including handles containing spaces or punctuation. Do not introduce recipient-list parsing into Internet addresses.

After explicit approval, save one ordinary local letter per recipient in one transaction. Each copy has its own stable ID, mail number, correspondent context and recipient confirmation. The sender can inspect every copy. This is a bounded local reconstruction, without a claim to implement the historical capacity.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction

Sources inspected live on 2026-10-24:

- [NEC PC-VAN office account, March 1993, printed p. 231](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/43/3/43_KJ00002959297/_pdf/-char/ja) explicitly documents simultaneous distribution to up to 100 recipients. Confidence is high for that earlier capability. Continuity into late 1996 is an accepted moderate-confidence inference. PDF text was readable, with damaged OCR spacing; page-image retrieval failed.
- [CROCUS author description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win31/net/se014206.html) explicitly lists multiple-recipient mail in indexed text. Direct retrieval failed. This is supplementary, snippet-only corroboration with unresolved feature dating, not evidence of host syntax or recipient visibility. The previously identified catalog-date page also remained inaccessible; no new dating conclusion was obtained.
- [Internet Magazine, November 1996, printed p. 221](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199611-220-mail2.pdf) documents PC-VAN Internet-mail addressing using `INET#`. It establishes a separate existing journey to preserve, without supplying the local multi-recipient composer.

Focused searches did not recover a qualifying target-year selection sequence, recipient-visibility rule or sent-mail layout. Indexed ECOM postal distribution and older inter-network addressing were kept separate from ordinary local mail.

**Accepted category D reconstruction:** `WRITE-MULTI`, repeated address entry, `.END`, local roster bounds, review layout, separate per-recipient copies, atomic browser persistence and contextual returns. Recipient copies expose their own correspondence only; do not describe this as authenticated BCC behavior. Exact historical controls, CC/BCC and reply-all remain unresolved. Use original fictional examples without copying historical identities, messages or images.

### Implementation and existing evidence

The checkout matches the baseline, has a clean worktree and has the same tree as PR #118's implementation head.

Relevant code:

- `src/commands.ts:startCompose` resolves and pins one recipient before creating `TerminalComposer`; `recordsHistory` and `invalidate()` protect active input and world replacement.
- `src/composer.ts` already provides literal multiline input, review, text editing, explicit approval, cancellation, retry and consumed-send behavior. Its save result and success output currently assume one mail number.
- `src/storage/schema.ts:resolveMailResident` preserves stable-address precedence and rejects ambiguous handles. `validateMailRelations` enforces pair-specific parents and confirmation evidence.
- `src/storage/repository.ts:createHumanMail`, `insertMail` and `transaction` provide validated writes, monotonic numbering, rollback and reset/restore generation fences. Calling the single-letter API repeatedly would allow partial delivery; use one transaction for the complete selection.
- `src/ai/mail.ts:pairMail` restricts memory to the human/resident pair. Preserve that boundary.

Live repository queries returned no open Issues or PRs. Searches for multi-recipient, broadcast, 同報 and multiple recipients found related earlier mail and ECOM scopes without an equivalent handoff. [Issue #52](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/52) establishes resident-mail privacy and shared identities; [#93](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/93) explicitly deferred multiple recipients for Internet mail; [#101](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/101) concerns a separate postal service.

[PR #118](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/118) and `docs/validation.md` report 123 focused and 457 complete-suite passing checks with three workers, including configured TypeScript checking and production bundling. They disclose earlier timing failures that passed unchanged on recheck. These are Coordinator records, not checks performed by this research graph; timing reliability remains unresolved.

Scope is new multi-recipient plain-text mail to existing local residents. Internet multi-address delivery, attachments, scheduled delivery, reply-all, group conversations, mailbox migration and unrelated service expansion remain deferred.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Make `WRITE-MULTI` discoverable in existing mail help and address guidance across all three mail routes. Require/select the existing human identity through the established registration flow, then collect individual resident destinations. Preserve each route's actual return context.
- [ ] Resolve addresses through existing local rules. Reject unknown, ambiguous, human, external and duplicate destinations without losing accepted selections. Different aliases for the same resident count as duplicates. `.END` requires at least two distinct eligible residents; the available roster bounds the selection. HELP/MEMBERS retain selection, cancellation discards it, and attempted navigation explains how to cancel. Do not reinterpret existing single-recipient syntax or synthetic display tokens.
- [ ] Pin resolved recipient IDs and safe display labels when selected. Opening and every review show all recipients distinctly. Renames or member reordering cannot silently retarget a draft. Revalidate recipient existence/eligibility during saving. Recipient changes can use explicit cancellation and restarted selection; text editing retains the pinned selection.
- [ ] Reuse the existing subject/body limits, literal Japanese multiline input, `.TEXT`, review, EDIT and cancellation semantics. Only explicit approval of the reviewed draft saves copies. Simulated IME confirmation, empty input, HELP, unrelated commands and repeated queued approval cannot send accidentally. Include the selection state in command-history exclusion and input-ownership guards.
- [ ] Save all copies and allocate their unique monotonic numbers within one existing IndexedDB transaction. Validate the whole request and every copy. Quota, validation or transaction failure after an earlier copy was inserted must roll back all copies and number allocation, leaving the draft retryable. Do not implement this as sequential calls to `createHumanMail`.
- [ ] Assign stable retry identities before saving. Identical concurrent retries produce one complete set; reused identities with conflicting content or recipients fail. Preserve numbering under concurrent ordinary, Internet and multi-recipient saves. After commitment, consume the entire draft even if refresh/rendering fails. Success output identifies every saved copy and its number rather than reporting only the first.
- [ ] SENT and READ show each copy's own recipient, exact subject/body, existing identity presentation and historical date projection. Copies survive reload and JSON export/import; legacy backups and deliberately empty mailboxes remain valid. Prefer existing Mail rows and validation without a new group-message subsystem. Any necessary stored fields require strict write/import validation and documented compatibility.
- [ ] Preserve separate correspondent memory, reply parents and confirmation evidence. A resident reply can confirm only its explicit parent copy; another copy remains unconfirmed. Co-recipient lists, other recipients' private letters and batch bookkeeping must not enter resident, forum or OLT prompts. Common text intentionally sent to several residents may appear independently in each pair. Preserve existing consent, scheduling, generation limits and public-work capacity; sending must not trigger a model download or guarantee replies.
- [ ] Reset/restore/world replacement invalidates recipient selection and reviewed drafts across tabs, including identical-JSON restore. Stale queued input cannot save into the replacement world. Preserve unrelated posts, read states, conference, OLT, NetNews, resident settings and consent; normal session/activity bookkeeping may continue. The journey causes no external mail request or mail-client handoff.
- [ ] Extend existing Playwright coverage and helpers. Repository cases must cover duplicate aliases, invalid recipients, complete-set retries, concurrent numbering, rollback after an earlier copy write, collision rejection, legacy/JSON round-trip and stale-world fences. Controller/production cases must cover all three callers, registration, selection cancellation, pinned identities, exact Japanese text, review/edit/approve, SENT/READ, reload, failed-save retry, post-commit refresh failure and simulated IME protection. Use existing mocked inference to verify pair isolation and independent explicit-parent confirmations. Preserve current functional, storage, consent, privacy, IME and terminal regression coverage.
- [ ] Update `docs/mail.md`, the historical research record, relevant README/About text and storage documentation where affected. Record URLs, inspection dates, access limitations, confidence and reconstruction assumptions. Document separate copies, local roster scope, backups/logs and unsent-draft lifetime. Keep detailed provenance on existing documentation/About surfaces.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs focused existing mail/composition/terminal coverage and the documented complete suite using `npm test -- --workers=3`; the existing configuration includes TypeScript checking and production bundling. Record actual worker count, failures, corrections and unperformed checks. Review the complete diff, affected links and `git diff --check`. No new framework, real model, human approval or hardware gate is required.

## Optional validation

Additional browser/native-IME checks or a newly recovered dated local-mail transcript may refine compatibility and presentation. They are not completion gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge.
